title: amygdalus elaeagrifolia var. kotschyi
intro: Amygdalus elaeagrifolia var. kotschyi, commonly known as Wild Apricot, is a deciduous shrub or small tree native to the mountainous regions of the Middle East and Central Asia. The health benefits of Wild Apricot include its ability to act as an antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial agent, which may help to protect against chronic diseases such as cardiovascular disease, cancer, and neurodegenerative disorders. The therapeutic actions of Wild Apricot include its use as an anti-anxiety, anti-depressant, and anti-aging agent, due to its bioactive constituents which include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and essential oils. The bioactive constituents of Wild Apricot have been found to include flavonoids such as kaempferol and quercetin, as well as phenolic acids like chlorogenic acid and ferulic acid.
